name: hpo_to_adverse_terms
built_by: hand-written in experiment E5+E6 (entry 152); every MedDRA id verified against OnSIDES v3.1.1 vocab_meddra_adverse_effect.csv on 2026-09-24 and confirmed to occur on at least one label
method: The child's 8 clinical HPO terms were read one by one against the MedDRA terms OnSIDES actually uses. For each HPO term the candidate label terms were found by case-insensitive regex over vocab_meddra_adverse_effect.csv (patterns recorded in entry 152), then kept or dropped by hand. Each kept row carries a tier: exact = the same event; class = a parent or sibling on the same clinical axis; precursor = a mechanistic antecedent. used_for_flag = no means the row is recorded but excluded from the drug flag, with the reason in rationale.

sources.clinical: ressources/hackathon-rules/Challenge_Clinical_Phenotype_1.md - the proband's 8 HPO terms; the 8th (HP:0200067) is the parents' reproductive history and is excluded
sources.genomic: none - this table is clinical only; it is joined to the genomic side in ressources/track2/candidate_safety.tsv

inputs.name: OnSIDES v3.1.1
inputs.role: the MedDRA vocabulary the labels are coded in

inputs.name: CPIC statin guideline (PMID 35152405)
inputs.role: fixes 'Myopathy' as the label term for statin-associated musculoskeletal symptoms

inputs.name: Fayard 2022 (PMID 35348900)
inputs.role: fixes hypercalciuria as the mechanistic precursor of nephrocalcinosis in preterm infants; contradicted by PMID 30473868, see entry 152

columns.used_for_flag: yes = the id is in the set used to match labels; no = recorded for inspection only
columns.decided_by: who made the judgement and where it is argued

assumptions: a label term on the same clinical axis as a patient phenotype is treated as a potential collision; MedDRA PT is preferred over LLT; the mapping is a judgement call, which is why every row carries its rationale
limitations: no HPO-to-MedDRA standard mapping exists, so this is manual and not reusable without review for another patient; 'Weight decreased' and 'Rhabdomyolysis' are broad, high-base-rate terms, which is exactly what the matched comparison set in candidate_safety.tsv exists to correct for; 'Premature birth' has no defensible label term and is excluded
validation: positive control - furosemide, the one drug with a published nephrocalcinosis association in preterm infants (PMID 35348900), is matched by this mapping (5 of 164 labels, Nephrocalcinosis + Nephrolithiasis); calcitriol is matched on Calculus urinary. Entry 152 records both.
